notes.note:
Key feedback for the designers:

- I was at A6 when the game started, and the engine status visible to me included `treasure=A6` even before I dug. That leaks the hidden treasure location. If the goal is for digging/searching to matter, the treasure coordinate should not be exposed in the status until the cave is revealed.
- My strategy once I found the cave: dig, write a one-line scroll message telling the other pirates the cave is at A6, then enter on the next available turn. Spending one turn to communicate cost 10 points, but it was clearly worth it because it lets the other pirates come straight to the entrance and score their own 100 + turn bonus.
- I entered promptly rather than hovering at the cave. Staying on the cave square blocks other pirates from entering and also costs 10 points per delay, so there is no reason to wait after posting the message.
- I didn’t use `read` because I already had the critical information; the scroll was for sending, not receiving.

Overall, the main strategic lesson: communicate the cave location immediately, then enter as soon as possible to free the entrance and maximize the turns-left bonus.

As pirate-2, I read the scroll on my first turn and it was empty. On my second turn I read again and found pirate-1's message: the treasure cave was open at A6. I moved north to A6 and entered. Entering on my 4th turn left me with 20 turns remaining, so my contribution was 100 + 20×10 = 300 toward the crew bounty.

The main lesson: early reading was valuable because the scroll was the only coordination channel, and pirate-1 used it correctly to announce the cave location. Once the message was seen, the correct action was simply to go to A6 and enter immediately.

Designers: The key moment was the scroll message from Pirate-1 saying the treasure cave was at A6 and open. Since we’re scored as a crew, there was no reason for Pirate-1 to lie, so I trusted it. I didn’t waste a turn reading the scroll again; I just headed to A6. When I arrived on A6, my position confirmed it was the open cave, so I entered immediately. I used 6 turns total, so I entered with 18 turns remaining.

Possible notes:
- The scroll is powerful: a single truthful message can end the search phase and coordinate everyone efficiently.
- Trusting a crewmate’s message is correct under cooperative scoring, but if the game ever included misleading messages, pirates would need verification or a protocol.
- Reading too often costs turns; I read once after the first two crew turns, which was enough.
- The fastest interception of an early cave reveal is important; in this case, moving north through B5/B6 then west to A6 worked.

The game was straightforward because Pirate-1 found the cave early and wrote its location to the scroll. I read the message, trusted it, traveled to A6, and entered. Since this is a cooperative scoring setup, sharing the exact cave location as soon as it is found is the highest-value use of the scroll. One design note: since reading and writing cost turns, it might be interesting to test how much coordination should happen before a cave is found, and whether players can afford to check the scroll regularly or should search for a fixed number of turns first.
